chapter.title: Probability Logics and Alternative Representations of Belief

sections.title: Belief functions, possibility measures and their distinct combination assumptions

missing_pieces.duty: assessment_dispute: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-7-C02: Missing from the source's sec.4.3 decision-rule argument (printed p.313): the maxmin rule LP(f)>=LP(g) is offered as resolving the Ellsberg paradox, while robust preference LP(f-g)>0 satisfies Savage's sure-thing principle. thm:p15-r47-price-boundaries (body 467-475, annex 170-182) separates the two rules but never states or bounds this contrast. Also missing from the sec.4.1 Cox critique (p.310): postulate (i) is natural only if Bayes conditioning is presupposed, and Paris's proof uses a weaker condition (iii), F strictly increasing in each argument. Body 327-333 gives only 'additional infinite/density assumptions'.

assessment_dispute: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-7-C03: Missing historical claims about evidence theory and Dempster's rule. These are: Shafer's theory as an interpretation of Dempster's upper/lower probabilities, or as a revival of the Bernoulli-Lambert probability of testimony (p.311); the 17th/18th-century pioneers' special cases of Dempster's rule, including the p1+p2-p1p2 reinforcement (p.312); and Bernoulli/Lambert's non-additive degrees of belief (p.306). Body 339-421 gives the rule only in formal terms, so it does not separate the historical and formal status of the rule's origin.

assessment_dispute: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-7-C05: The source's claim (p.313) that the lower-prevision maxmin rule solves the Ellsberg paradox while LP(f-g)>0 satisfies the sure-thing principle is not proved, not cited to a fixed dependent source and not bounded on the route.

assessment_dispute: X-165.8-title-combination-assumptions: The route states Dempster combination's assumptions: independence, nonempty-intersection normalization, K>0 and the dependent-copy failure (body 389-413, annex 128-143). It does not give a possibilistic rule for combining sources or that rule's assumptions to contrast with them. So 'their distinct combination assumptions' is supplied only for belief functions.
